body:
Raised 2026-10-06 (America/Los_Angeles) by post-merge Auditor `01a10892-0782-7b13-902c-d8b4db6c155d`. Parent #420 / regional umbrella #415; affected PR #1004, merge `96f2a6d201236ba62f471535db240b123de60c09`, head `cf4892e18f5515e1f9d42833c0ca64ec9244ba4e`.

The retained `data/regional-review/regional-review-c64d17e99f61d668/reproduce_crosswalk.py` validates its retained source-manifest files but reads Atlas geography from filesystem `part-*.json` without an immutable Atlas/code baseline guard. Its `atlas[key]=props` and `source[key]=...` maps replace repeated subject IDs before the later set-equality checks. Finally it unconditionally rewrites the historical `crosswalk.json` with the fixed historical retrieval date. A successful 207-row run therefore does not prove the original Atlas baseline was used or every input subject occurred exactly once, and it can replace the retained result.

The Auditor executed two actual isolated, immutable-merge runs after redirecting only that historical write to exclusive private outputs. Both reproduce the original 536,887-byte crosswalk exactly, SHA256 `5c231dddec6314f50dbf18df3a55f5bd2fe0d74b7ddd51189650d2914fe749ec`. Original bytes are unchanged. This is a safeguard defect, not a claim that the retained numerical output is wrong.

Two actual synthetic-input probes against the retained runner demonstrate the failure:

1. At the `Path.read_text` boundary for the complete pinned `data/geography/part-9.json`, change only the name of `gb:GRC:ADM3:53547021B78625637491486` to `AUDITOR_SYNTHETIC_BASELINE_DRIFT`. The runner completes with 207 rows and emits that changed name under its unchanged dated result. Output SHA256 `f7ec290081e6dcd78c39c13e5e108ec5b3f920389be86ed5888c22ebadf480c1`.
2. Separately append a duplicate of that complete original feature to the same full part at that read boundary. The runner accepts both occurrences and emits the byte-identical original crosswalk: its dictionary silently collapses the duplicate. Both probes intercepted only the read and redirected the final output; no actual original, source or retained packet was modified. The complete synthetic parts were 6,115,310 and 6,118,881 bytes, and each complete probe remained under 256 MiB.

Expected: validate exact immutable complete inputs and reject changed/wrong-baseline/code/source bytes or duplicate native/source subjects before emitting a result. Retained original evidence must remain immutable; corrective runs require exclusive fresh versioned outputs with distinct historical-source and actual-execution provenance.

Bounded work, at most two PRs, only in `data/regional-review/southeastern-europe-reproduction-420-erratum/`:

- Add a separate runner/erratum that pins the cited immutable merge and every complete consumed original Atlas/source/packet/code input, verifies subject occurrences before dictionary construction, and checks exact IDs/parents and complete whole-file accounting. Use the 61 actual complete-input descriptors below; avoid a selective fragment masquerading as an original. Do not edit the old scripts, crosswalk, source extracts or other workers' packets.
- Execute two runs to distinct fresh exclusive outputs, compare against the preserved historical crosswalk, and retain meaningful rejection controls for changed Atlas geometry/metadata/baseline/code/source, duplicate Atlas/source IDs and existing output. Record any real result difference separately rather than relabeling old evidence. Distinguish observation/retrieval dates from execution time. Preserve all classifications, original raw/derived sources, stable IDs/parents and the explicit DGU/Greek source limitations. Obtain substantive exact-head source/implementation review and applicable gates.

Success: exact 207 native subject roster and ten original province workload contexts; no silent duplicate collapse or mutable baseline substitution; old bytes/hash unchanged; two genuinely complete deterministic corrected runs and meaningful negative controls; manifest pins/owned change accounting and actual complete-phase sizes within 32 MiB per object, 256 MiB per phase and 512 descriptors. Original mechanical reproduction used 236,953,157 ordinary input bytes and a 239,586,874-byte complete-phase admission including release decode and two MiB output reserve. Recalculate admission for the new runner/evidence; do not weaken the limits.

Readiness reviewed: #420 is closed and its canonical author claim was released. Complete open/closed issue and open-PR pagination found no existing scoped reproduction erratum or ownership of the new path. #1002 (80 Greek authoritative-boundary restoration) and #1003 (Magadenovac identity/boundary) are open and preserve their own paths/claims; this work does not duplicate or expand them. No regional approval dependency is needed for this source-only reproduction safeguard. Exactly 207 native subject IDs are declared below; the ten hierarchy parent contexts remain original inputs, not subjects for a parent edit or new approval.

Limits: the Auditor independently verified complete original-world identity, 207 source/current geometry hashes, all province counts, retained CSV classifications and exact upstream GitHub object identities for the two geoBoundaries geometry/metadata pairs. The XLS-to-CSV conversion, DGU 208,774,354-byte archive/600,770,112-byte GML and missing official primary-page bodies are not independently authenticated here. This follow-up does not restore or certify those sources, resolve licenses, approve boundaries/parent meaning, run the oversized extractor, alter core geography/releases/facts, import, deploy or authorize publisher operations. Missing scientific verification remains on the original PR's Incomplete audit.
